LOS ANGELES, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Asian World Film Festival (AWFF) today unveiled the details of its 2026 Focus On Taiwan program, which will take place on Nov. 14, 2026 at the Culver Theater in Culver City, California. The half-day celebration of Taiwanese cinema will present four award-winning films—a feature film and three shorts—red carpet arrivals, and audience Q&As.

"From the animated world of 'Praying Mantis' to the intimate portrait of Taiwan past in 'A Foggy Tale," Focus On Taiwan provides audiences with a sense of the sweep of Taiwanese cinema," said Georges N. Chamchoum, AWFF executive director. "Taiwan has long inspired filmmakers beyond its borders and it's a joy to present work that continues that tradition."

"This year, TAICCA is presenting 'A Foggy Tale,' Taiwan's official Oscar entry, which earned more than US$3 million at the Taiwan box office, along with three Oscar-qualified shorts that reflect the depth and range of Taiwanese filmmaking across different forms," said Sue Wang, chairperson of the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA). "The Asian World Film Festival is an important North American stage during awards season, and we hope it will help more Academy members discover Taiwanese stories."

Focus on Taiwan will open with a trio of shorts that have qualified for Academy Award consideration, each winning in a different category—animation, live action and documentary. "Praying Mantis," directed by Hsieh Wen-ming (Joe), comes to the festival after receiving both the Golden Horse Award for Best Animated Short Film and the Grand Prize for Short Animation at the Ottawa International Animation Festival. Huang Sheng Chun's live action "The Brave Swing" won the Best International Fiction Award at the Odense International Film Festival. And, Hsu Hui-ju's "Fragments of Herstory," garnered the Golden Horse Award for Best Documentary Short Film.

Closing the day will be "A Foggy Tale," Chen Yu-Hsun's poignant drama set in mid-20th century Taiwan. The film won four honors at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards, including Best Narrative Feature, and was selected as the Taiwanese entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards.

Focus On Taiwan is presented in collaboration with the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA) and the Taiwan Academy in Los Angeles.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Notefinder launched today on the web and iPad, giving musicians a new place to find high-quality, fully licensed sheet music in the most popular formats.

Licensed, publisher-quality arrangements

Every arrangement on Notefinder is professionally created and licensed from the publishers, so songwriters are paid on every purchase. Notefinder comes from sheet music publisher Music, Inc., which has licensing deals with more than 1,400 rights holders, including the majors. The catalog includes music by artists such as Adele, Coldplay, Olivia Rodrigo, Radiohead and Billie Eilish.

"Low-quality sheet music doesn't meet the needs of the musician, respect the publisher or capture the artist's intent. We built Notefinder on a promise of quality and trust, from every score to the service as a whole," said Jonathan Kehl, CEO, Music, Inc.

A Rock Band format for cover bands

Notefinder's Rock Band format is made for cover bands and gigging musicians. Instead of a note-for-note transcription, each arrangement is designed for a typical cover band, with a full score and parts for vocals, guitars, keyboard, bass and drums at three levels, plus practical performance notes. It launches alongside Piano / Vocal / Guitar, Piano / Vocal and Solo Piano, with more formats coming soon.

Buy one score, or subscribe to them all

      • Single score: $4.99 as a PDF download to print and keep
      • Subscription: $7.99 a month or $49.99 a year for the entire catalog, including interactive versions of every score, with a 7-day free trial 

        Interactive scores play back as you read, and muting the vocal part turns them into practice tracks for singers. Prices shown are for the US.

A free score reader for iPad

The Notefinder iPad app is free, with no account or purchase required. Musicians can import their own PDFs, add scores from Notefinder, or both, and their whole library works offline.

"The market has been missing a score reader that is free, dependable and able to work with the music people already own. With Notefinder, musicians can bring their own PDFs, use them offline and add to their library from a catalog they can trust, through a single purchase or a subscription," said Martin Keary, Chief Product Officer, Music, Inc.

Classical favorites for free

Popular works by Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Chopin and other composers are free on Notefinder.

Localized for 10 markets

Notefinder is localized for the United States, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Brazil, Japan, South Korea and China.

Availability

Notefinder is available now at notefinder.com and on iPad (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/notefinder-sheet-music-reader/id6810637456). An Android app is coming soon.

Notefinder is a sheet music store and score reader app from Music, Inc., offering licensed, publisher-quality arrangements on the web and iPad, localized for 10 markets.

Music, Inc. creates high-quality arrangements of licensed sheet music in the most popular formats.

releases.title: The Ballpark That Forever Changed the Game of Baseball: New Film from The Babe Ruth Birthplace & Museum Takes Fans Behind the Scenes to See the Creation of Oriole Park at Camden Yards
releases.body:
Documentary made possible by the Lucchino Family Foundation in memory of former Orioles president Larry Lucchino, will debut at a private screening Nov. 14; public premiere set for Babe Ruth's 132nd birthday in February 2027

BALTIMORE, Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Babe Ruth Birthplace and Museum will debut a new documentary about the making of Oriole Park at Camden Yards, "The Ballpark That Forever Changed the Game of Baseball," at a private screening Saturday, Nov. 14. The premiere will be held at the Camden Club in the B&O Warehouse at Camden Yards. The film will premiere publicly on Feb. 6, 2027, coinciding with what would have been Babe Ruth's 132nd birthday, at the museum's newly renovated theater.

The 20-minute film follows the ballpark from concept in the 1980s to Opening Day in 1992 through first-hand interviews, covering site selection, architectural choices and how the park got its name. It closes with the ballpark's legacy, highlighting how Baltimore's new retro park redefined ballpark design and ushered in a new era of stadium development across Major League Baseball. Those interviewed include Hall of Fame broadcaster Jon Miller; Orioles legend and Hall of Famer Cal Ripken Jr.; and Janet Marie Smith, who represented the Orioles on the ballpark design. The film is narrated by Orioles play-by-play broadcaster Kevin Brown.

Columnist George Will has ranked Oriole Park at Camden Yards among baseball's most significant developments since World War II, alongside Jackie Robinson's breaking of the color barrier in 1947 and the arrival of free agency.

The film was made possible by the Lucchino Family Foundation in memory of former Orioles president Larry Lucchino, whose vision and leadership helped bring Oriole Park at Camden Yards to life. As Orioles president from 1988 to 1993, Lucchino played a pivotal role in championing a new ballpark that would reconnect the team with downtown Baltimore and fundamentally change the way baseball stadiums were designed. Lucchino died in 2024.

His clear vision and constant mantra to build "an old-fashioned ballpark with modern amenities" guided the development of the ballpark from start to finish. The film includes archival interview footage of Lucchino, offering audiences the opportunity to hear directly from one of the key figures behind the ballpark's creation.

The Lucchino Family Foundation's support of the documentary reflects its commitment to honoring Larry's enduring contributions to baseball and ensuring that his legacy and impact on the game continue to be recognized by future generations.

"Camden Yards was one of the defining accomplishments of my uncle's career, and its impact on baseball has been felt far beyond Baltimore," said David Lucchino, Trustee, the Lucchino Family Foundation. "Larry believed in doing things differently, challenging convention and creating something that would stand the test of time. The ballpark helped change the way generations of fans experience the game, and we're proud that the Lucchino Family Foundation could help bring this film to life. It's an important opportunity to preserve the story behind Camden Yards and ensure that Larry's vision, along with the contributions of everyone who helped make it possible, is remembered for generations to come."

The film features interviews with Janet Marie Smith, represented the Orioles on the ballpark design; Hall of Fame broadcaster Jon Miller; and Orioles legend and Hall of Famer Cal Ripken Jr. Orioles play-by-play broadcaster Kevin Brown narrates. The film was produced by Baltimore's Aliceanna Collective.

Members of the Lucchino family, community leaders and representatives of Major League Baseball and the Baltimore Orioles are among those invited to attend the Nov. 14 screening.

"The film captures the behind-the-scenes story of how Oriole Park at Camden Yards came to be," said museum spokesperson Mike Gibbons. "It's widely considered the most important ballpark in baseball architecture since Yankee Stadium, 'the House that Ruth Built.'"

The museum is planning additional private screenings ahead of the February public premiere. The renovated museum theater features an old-time scoreboard and a new playback system. The Babe Ruth Museum maintained full editorial control over the production of the film. The film was produced by Baltimore's Aliceanna Collective.

About the Babe Ruth Birthplace Foundation

The Babe Ruth Birthplace Foundation, Inc. is an independent, not-for-profit educational institution dedicated to perpetuating the historic legacy of Babe Ruth, Baltimore's Orioles, Ravens and Colts, and local and regional sports at the amateur, collegiate and professional levels, by preserving, exhibiting, interpreting and augmenting its collection for a diverse audience. For more information visit baberuthmuseum.org.

About the Lucchino Family Foundation

Established by pioneering baseball executive and philanthropist Larry Lucchino, the Lucchino Family Foundation carries forward his enduring commitment to healthcare, education and community enrichment. The Foundation supports organizations and initiatives that advance cancer research and treatment, expand educational opportunities for future generations, and improve the quality of life in communities, particularly those with the greatest need. Guided by Larry's values of hard work, excellence, family and service, the Foundation prioritizes meaningful, measurable impact while honoring his extraordinary legacy in professional baseball and his lifelong dedication to making a difference in the lives of others.

releases.body:
WINTER PARK, Fla., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Full Sail University has been named one of the Top 50 Film Schools of 2026 by TheWrap magazine, the publication's annual ranking of leading film education institutions.

Full Sail University Named to TheWrap Magazine's Top 50 Film Schools of 2026

TheWrap's 11th annual ranking recognizes colleges and universities that demonstrate excellence in preparing students for careers in filmmaking and the broader entertainment industry. The data-driven evaluation considers factors including curriculum, faculty qualifications, production equipment, hands-on filmmaking opportunities, industry connections, facilities and more.

Full Sail University's inclusion reflects its approach to creative education, which combines project-based learning, professional production environments, emerging technologies, and collaboration across multiple areas of entertainment media.

"We are honored to be recognized by TheWrap among the nation's leading film schools," said Rick Ramsey, Education Director for Visual Arts at Full Sail University. "Our commitment is to give aspiring filmmakers opportunities to develop their creative voices while gaining practical experience with the tools, technologies, and collaborative production environments that are shaping today's entertainment industry. Our students don't simply study filmmaking – they actively create, produce, and bring their stories to life."

Full Sail University offers a range of film and cinematography programs designed to help students develop the creative, technical, and production-management skills needed across today's film, television and media landscape.

Full Sail's film-focused academic offerings include:

  • Film Bachelor of Science: An immersive, project-based program that introduces students to the complete filmmaking process, including screenwriting, pre-production, directing, cinematography, production design, camera operation, editing, sound, and post-production.
  • Film Production Master of Fine Arts: An advanced, project-based graduate program focused on visual storytelling, screenwriting, directing, producing, cinematography, editing, sound, and professional development. Students build their expertise through collaborative productions and graduate-level filmmaking.
  • Digital Cinematography Bachelor of Science: An online degree program focused on digital filmmaking, camera operation, lighting, audio, field production, editing, and visual storytelling. Students develop the skills to create professional content for independent film, broadcast, commercial, and digital media platforms.

In addition, Full Sail's is home to extensive campus production facilities. Located in Winter Park, Florida, the university's over 210-acre campus features more than 880,000 square feet of real-world production spaces, including more than 110 studios and labs.

Key facilities include:

  • Full Sail Backlot: A Hollywood-style outdoor production environment located on-campus featuring a variety of scenic facades and backdrops that allow students to experience location-based filmmaking and production design.
  • Studio V1: Virtual Production Studio: A dedicated virtual production environment that introduces students to emerging production techniques and the integration of physical and digital filmmaking environments.
  • Film Soundstages: Dedicated spaces for filming, set construction, lighting, camera operation, and collaborative production work.
  • The Dub Stage: A theatrical mixing facility designed to mirror professional post-production sound workflows, giving students experience with the audio processes involved in preparing content for theatrical presentation.
  • Spatial Computing Innovation Lab: An advanced creative technology environment that introduces students to the latest in immersive media technology. This lab is the first collegiate environment in the nation to be outfitted with the Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive camera for use with Apple Vision Pro.

Through access to these facilities, students can experience the filmmaking process in environments that encourage experimentation, collaboration, and practical skill development. Students also utilize Project LaunchBox™, a technology package featuring hardware and software customized to their degree program.

Full Sail's film graduates have contributed to notable and award-winning productions and projects across the entertainment industry, with alumni working on projects associated with major studios, streaming platforms, and production companies, including Universal, Paramount, Hulu, and more.

This recent recognition from TheWrap adds to Full Sail University's continued presence in national film school rankings and reinforces its commitment to preparing the next generation of filmmakers through hands-on education, creative collaboration, and access to professional-style production environments.

To learn more about Full Sail University's Film and Television degree programs, visit the university's website.

About Full Sail University:

Full Sail University is an award-winning educational leader for those pursuing careers in entertainment media and emerging technologies. Founded in 1979, Full Sail has received numerous accolades throughout its over 45-year history, including most recently being named a 2026 "Top Game Design School" by The Princeton Review and one of "The 30 Best Film Schools in the U.S. and Canada" in 2026 by MovieMaker Magazine. Full Sail University is a graduate and undergraduate degree-granting institution offering on-campus and online degree programs in areas related to Art & Design, Business, Film & Television, Games, Media & Communications, Music & Recording, Sports, and Technology. With over 100,000 graduates worldwide, Full Sail alumni have worked on countless award-winning projects with individual recognition including Oscar®, Emmy®, Grammy®, Addy® and The Game Award honors.

releases.title: Abbeville Press Publishes Book Featuring Iconic Artifacts and Images from the Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum's Collection
releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Abbeville Press and the Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum have collaborated to publish a new, lavishly illustrated book showcasing iconic artifacts, rare documents and images from the museum's collection. Treasures of the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum (Abbeville Press) tells the story of country music through the objects and artists that define it, spanning its pre-commercial roots to the present day. The book is now available in time for the holidays in bookstores and retail outlets nationwide, as well as through the museum's store.

Published in an oversize square format the size of an LP jacket, the 348-page book includes vibrant photographs that bring readers up close to many of the music's most important artifacts, as well as lively narrative by the museum's staff of historians and writers. It is edited by the museum's Senior Director of Editorial Paul Kingsbury and features a foreword by Oscar- and Grammy-winning composer, producer and songwriter T Bone Burnett.

"The Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum is an archeological exploration into a unique music that has been developed in this country and its crucial contribution to the soul of this country," writes Burnett. "Since 1967, the museum has been telling the story of our country principally through the subjects of the photographs you see in this book — treasures of country music — which were once the instruments and implements that working-class people used to turn their sorrows and joys into song."

Some artists and artifacts featured include:

  • DeFord Bailey – Hohner Marine Band harmonica and his home-made megaphone to amplify his sound. Bailey was an influential harmonica player and country music's first Black star.
  • Maybelle Carter – the 1928 Gibson L-5 arch-top guitar, which she played throughout most of her career.
  • Bill Monroe – the Gibson F-5 Master Model the "Father of Bluegrass" played almost his entire career. It was built in 1923 by Gibson's legendary acoustic engineer, Lloyd Loar.
  • Earl Scruggs – 1930 Gibson RB-Granada Mastertone five-string banjo, acquired in a 1949 trade with fellow bluegrass star Don Reno, and which became Scruggs' main instrument.
  • Rose Maddox – three-piece, heavily embroidered red-and-yellow cowgirl outfit, designed by Nathan Turk.
  • Johnny Cash – the first black suit worn onstage by "The Man in Black," which features silver trim sewn on by his mother, c. 1955.
  • Minnie Pearl – the thrift-store straw hat with plastic flowers and a dangling price tag she wore at the Grand Ole Opry.
  • Hank Williams – original two-page, handwritten (with his corrections) song manuscript for "I Saw the Light" from 1947.
  • Dolly Parton – her early, handwritten draft of the lyrics to her 1973 #1 hit "Jolene."
  • Gram Parsons – "Nudie suit" with embroidered marijuana leaves, pills, poppies, and a cross on the back, which he wore on the cover of the Flying Burrito Brothers' debut album, The Gilded Palace of Sin (1969).
  • Emmylou Harris – embroidered and fringed tunic with blue jeans, which she wore on the cover of her 1975 album Elite Hotel.
  • Charley Pride – the 1967 Fender Coronado II hollow-body electric guitar with distinctive "Antigua" sunburst finish, which he used extensively in the 1960s and '70s.
  • Garth Brooks – striped Panhandle Slim western shirt, which he wore on the cover of his breakthrough, eighteen-times platinum album, No Fences (1990).
  • Shania Twain – Marc Bouwer-designed pink Ultrasuede outfit with matching hat and gloves, which she wore for her performance at the 1999 CMA Awards.
  • Jelly Roll – custom-made patchwork denim jacket, which he wore during his 2022 concert at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena.
  • Lainey Wilson - Lindsey Thornburg-designed silk halter top and pants worn by Wilson when she made her acting debut as Abby in Season Five of the television series "Yellowstone."

The book also features a selection of rare posters, publicity photos and behind-the-scenes snapshots to bring the personalities of country music to life. Other special features include biographies of all the members of the Country Music Hall of Fame and a curated playlist for every era of country music.

"When you look upon these one-of-a-kind wonders, consider the fact that you are beholding not only a beautiful museum collection, but tangible works of art that are associated with people who have often made themselves at home in our hearts and somehow become a part of all our lives," said Country Music Hall of Fame member Marty Stuart. 

"Abbeville Press is honored to have the opportunity to partner with the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum and celebrate their extraordinary collection, sharing the stories and artifacts that have shaped country music and inspired generations of artists and fans," said Cynthia Vance-Abrams, President. "We're delighted to bring these treasures from their home in 'Music City' to country music lovers everywhere with this richly illustrated and giftable volume."

The nonprofit Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the "Smithsonian of country music," recognized for its unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts, changing exhibits and educational programs. Its collection holds more than 500 historic instruments, 2,000 stage costumes, 300,000 records, 500,000 photographs and more. Many items are on display and rotated regularly as part of the museum's permanent exhibition Sing Me Back Home: A Journey Through Country Music. Read more about the museum's collection.

About the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum:

The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum collects, preserves and interprets country music and its history for the education and entertainment of diverse audiences. In exhibitions, publications, digital media and educational programs, the museum explores the cultural importance and enduring beauty of the art form. Among the most-visited history museums in the United States, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum was awarded the country's highest honor in the arts, the National Medal of Arts, in 2024. Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the museum is operated by the Country Music Foundation, a not-for-profit 501(c)(3) educational organization chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964. The Country Music Foundation operates Historic RCA Studio B®, Hatch Show Print® poster shop, Haley Gallery, CMA Theater, CMF Records, the Frist Library and Archive and CMF Press. More information about the Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum is available at www.countrymusichalloffame.org.

About Abbeville Press: 

Founded in 1977 by Harry N. Abrams and Robert E. Abrams, Abbeville Press is an independent publisher of fine art and illustrated books. Abbeville's books are distributed to the trade by W. W. Norton in North America and ACC Art Books elsewhere in the world. The Abbeville publishing program encompasses the oversize art books for which the imprint is best known; art, photography, and lifestyle books in a variety of smaller formats; select gift items and paper goods of the highest quality; and select children's nonfiction series. See the entire catalog online at www.abbeville.com.

RALEIGH, N.C., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Marcy Playground, managed by Deep South Entertainment, will join forces with Wheatus for a 2027 co-headlining tour, bringing two enduring alternative-rock acts to stages across the Eastern United States. The 19-date run begins March 18 in Washington, DC, and concludes April 10 in Nashville, TN.

The independent group has released six studio albums and two live albums while continuing to tour and perform at major festivals.

releases.body:
SPF26 convenes film, TV, music, and advertising professionals in Toronto on November 14 at CBC's Glenn Gould Studio, followed by four days of SPF Virtual. For its milestone 11th year, SPF26 marks several firsts: Accessibility Sponsors Telefilm Canada and the Disability Screen Office bring a new level of commitment to inclusivity, commercials and advertising join the program, and acclaimed musician and composer Donna Grantis delivers an exclusive live music performance. These additions signal a broader impact across the screen sector and highlight SPF26 as its most accessible and wide-ranging forum to date.

TORONTO, Nov. 10, 2026 /CNW/ -- The Sustainable Entertainment Society (SES) announces the return of the Sustainable Production Forum (SPF), the world's longest-running conference dedicated to sustainable screen production. Hosted by actor and writer Kudakwashe Rutendo, SPF26 adopts the theme "Horizons in Bloom," reflecting a sector that no longer questions the feasibility of sustainable production, and brings together producers, executives, department heads, crews, funders, vendors and sustainability experts.

The forum begins with a full in-person day on Saturday, November 14, 2026, at the Glenn Gould Studio and CBC Conference Centre in Toronto, starting with a Traditional Welcome from Luana Shirt (Plains Cree/Anishinaabe, Lynx Clan). Programming continues online with SPF Virtual on November 18, 21, 25, and 28, open to participants worldwide.

Since launching in 2016, SPF has welcomed more than 25,000 attendees, 1,000+ speakers, and 100+ partners across 500+ sessions. After Ontario Green Screen's report, Advancing Waste Management Practices in Ontario's Film and Television Industry, launched at SPF23, a working group formed to tackle storage, one of the stickiest barriers to reusing set materials. The new SOS Depot, getting its first look at SPF26, is the result of those long-standing efforts.

"Gathering, learning, and building confidence in this work should not be underestimated. SPF provides a firm foundation for momentum and progress so we do not become complacent," said Zena Harris, President, Green Spark Group.

SPF26 sets a new standard for accessibility. With Telefilm Canada and the Disability Screen Office's support, the forum now offers ASL interpretation, a wheelchair-accessible floorplan, flexible seating, a Low Stimulus Lounge, and closed captioning for the mainstage.

"Together with the Disability Screen Office, we're helping make accessibility an expectation, embedded in how Canada's screen industry plans and delivers screen industry events," said Elisa Suppa, Corporate Impact Director, Telefilm Canada.

In Toronto, panels explore climate storytelling with executives from CBC, Shaftesbury, and Cream Productions, alongside showrunner Morwyn Brebner; a look inside the new SOS Depot; and sustainability in advertising production. The day also includes workshops, Idea Boosts, and the Clean Energy Series, and concludes with Donna Grantis and Jennifer Baichwal in a fireside chat on humanNATURE, including a sneak peek of the upcoming Mercury Films documentary, followed by an exclusive live performance.

SPF Virtual features Indigenous filmmakers discussing traditional ecological knowledge, two global town halls, and a new green toolkit for animation. SPF26 also hosts Cohort 2 of SES's Sustainability Practitioners Internship Program (SPIP), with lead sponsor CBC.

"What I love most about SPF is the mix of people in the room: longtime changemakers who return each year, alongside new curious learners and planet enthusiasts finding their place in this work. I'm especially excited to bring our recently announced SPIP Cohort 2 on stage and introduce them to the community. They're proving that sustainability is a career path, not a side project," said Melanie Windle, Co-Founder and Executive Director, Sustainable Entertainment Society.

Tickets, speakers, and detailed programming: sustainableproductionforum.com. 

For media passes and coverage opportunities, contact melanie.windle@sustainableproductionforum.com. 

SPF26 is made possible with the support of partners: Government of Canada, Green Spark Group, Telefilm Canada, CBC/Radio-Canada, Ontario Green Screen, Independent Production Fund, City of Toronto, Canada Media Fund, Bell Fund, Bullfrog Power, Canadian Media Producers Association, Reel Green™, Sustainable Biz, Disability Screen Office, Canadian Film Centre, Producing for the Planet, Humber Polytechnic, Toronto Film School, B.I. Canada Works, Hone Inc., Krypton Rental Group, CTS Production Equipment, Driving Force, Stream Water, Muuse, MENA Film Festival, Sunbelt Rentals, Invest Durham, Centennial College, and GoodLot Farm.

About the Sustainable Entertainment Society

The Sustainable Entertainment Society (SES) is a Canadian non-profit advancing sustainability in arts and entertainment. SES produces the Sustainable Production Forum, the Clean Energy Series, and the Sustainability Practitioners Internship Program (SPIP).

releases.title: From Communism to the G20: New Film Shows Americans How Freedom Made Poland Thrive
releases.body:
WASHINGTON, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Poland is living proof that communism doesn't work and freedom does. Once Poles defeated Soviet-imposed communism in 1989, they were free to pursue their dreams, build businesses, and shape their own futures. That freedom unleashed the creativity, ambition, and entrepreneurial spirit of an entire nation, transforming Poland into one of Europe's fastest-growing economies.

On December 14–15, Poland will participate in the G20 Leaders' Summit in Miami for the first time ever, aiming to become a permanent member.

Yet many Americans still know Poland better for its history than its modern achievements. The National Polish American Foundation (NPAF) wants to change that.

To mark November 11, Poland's Independence Day and Veterans Day in the U.S., the foundation is releasing an English-language short film, "Freedom Is Worth Defending. Poland and the USA: From Saratoga to NATO."

Freedom Is Poland's Success Story

The video takes viewers from General Tadeusz Kościuszko at Saratoga and General Casimir Pulaski, the father of the American cavalry, through Poland's fight for independence and Solidarity to modern Poland.

Its message: Poland has always thrived when it was free. In under four decades, a struggling economy became a trillion-dollar one. Today, it leads NATO in defense spending relative to GDP.

"Americans have great respect for Poland and the Polish people, but many still see the country through the lens of history or outdated stereotypes. They don't always realize how much Poland has changed. Today, it has a strong economy, innovative companies, a growing technology sector, and one of the strongest militaries in Europe. We want more Americans, especially business leaders, investors, and policymakers, to see what modern Poland has to offer. The better we understand each other, the stronger our alliance will be," says Piotr Nowocień, founder and president of NPAF.

Building Poland's Brand Is a Job for Business

The video was produced by Big Dreams 4 Leaders (BD4L), a Warsaw-based agency that helps political and business leaders and organizations craft narratives that captivate audiences and change reality.

"South Korea, Japan and Ireland have spent years building their brands in the United States, and they are reaping the rewards in trade and investment. Polish business needs a strong Poland brand more than anyone," says Mateusz Sabat, CEO of BD4L.

BD4L proudly embraced the newest storytelling medium, powered by the latest technology.

"The technology let us bring Pulaski, Sobieski and the American pilots who fought for Poland in 1920 back to life," adds Anna Stypa, Partner and Head of PR & Customer Success at BD4L.

"The 9 million Americans with Polish roots are Poland's best ambassadors," says Nowocień.

Watch the video on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=STkOuVwwToA

About The National Polish American Foundation

The National Polish American Foundation is a Washington-based nonprofit that promotes the strategic partnership between Poland and the United States. Founded by Polish-born entrepreneur Piotr Nowocień. polamf.org

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Grab the popcorn but make it mini. MGA Entertainment (MGA) is changing the channel on collectibles with the launch of MGA's Miniverse Real TV Player and Video Tapes, a fully functional mini TV that plays collectible video tapes featuring clips from iconic movies and television shows.

Combining nostalgia, pop culture and the thrill of collecting, Miniverse Real TV lets fans build their own miniature entertainment library with more than 30 playable mini video tapes inspired by NBCUniversal's beloved entertainment brands including Amblin Entertainment and Universal Pictures' Back to the Future, DreamWorks Animation's Shrek and Kung Fu Panda as well as NBC and Peacock's The Office and Saved by the Bell, and more. Insert a video tape into the Real TV, press play and watch a 30-second clip, transforming each mini collectible into an interactive entertainment experience.

"The screen may be tiny, but the idea is anything but," said Josh Hackbarth, Chief Marketing Officer, MGA Entertainment. "Miniverse Real TV takes the movies and shows fans love and transforms them into a collection they can actually press play on. At a moment when fans are rediscovering the joy of physical media, there's something especially satisfying about choosing a video tape, inserting it into the TV and watching an iconic scene come to life. It blends nostalgia with real functionality in a way that feels playful, innovative, and completely unexpected, exactly what Miniverse does best."

MGA's Miniverse Real TV Player comes ready for its first mini watch party with a fully functional TV, one exclusive playable mini video tape, a mini TV stand and a mini video display case, all brought to life with detailed, retro-inspired styling.

The channel surfing continues with more than 30 Miniverse Real TV Video Tapes to collect. Sold separately in mystery capsules, each pack includes three playable mini video tapes featuring 30-second clips, plus a mini keychain for taking a favorite on the go. Together, the collection puts a playful, interactive spin on screen nostalgia, shrinking iconic entertainment into a format that is equal parts watchable and collectible.

MGA's Miniverse Real TV and Videos are available now at MGA Shop, with more retailers coming later this month. Fans can explore the entire MGA's Miniverse product collection at MGA Shop. Follow MGA's Miniverse on Instagram and TikTok.

About MGA Entertainment

MGA Entertainment is on a mission to inspire imagination and creativity through innovative toys, entertainment, and experiences that transform play into limitless possibilities. As the largest privately held toy and entertainment company in the U.S., MGA is a global leader in designing and delivering world-class consumer products that spark wonder and drive play forward. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices worldwide, MGA's portfolio spans a dynamic range of original and licensed brands — from toys, dolls, games, and electronics to fashion, home décor, and entertainment content including hit movies and TV series. The company is recognized for its bold approach to storytelling, trendsetting design, and deep commitment to quality. The award-winning MGA family includes fan-favorite brands such as L.O.L. Surprise!™, Little Tikes®, Rainbow High™, Bratz®, MGA's Miniverse™, Yummiland™, CarTuned™, Mirror Mi™, Ninjombie™, DohKins™, BABY born®, and Zapf Creation®. To learn more, visit www.mgae.com and follow MGA on LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram and Facebook.

releases.title: Rao's Homemade® Launches Moving Short Film Urging People to Make Time for Meals Together
releases.body:
The brand's new campaign reveals that time with loved ones is our most limited resource — and sharing a meal is the most meaningful way to reclaim it.

CAMDEN, N.J., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, Rao's Homemade is premiering the centerpiece of its Make Time.™ campaign: a captivating "Limited-Time Only" hero short film, directed by Aqsa + John X., the award-winning filmmakers behind Dove's landmark "Real Beauty Sketches." The short film delivers an emotional message — encouraging people to make more meaningful time together.

The short film is grounded in the reality that meals with family and friends have declined 25% over the last two decades*. Simply put, people are spending less meaningful time around the table. Rao's and Goodby Silverstein & Partners surveyed more than 1,000 individuals and conducted in-depth interviews with 200 people to explore mealtime habits and uncover who people miss connecting with most. From these conversations, three deeply personal stories were selected to anchor the campaign. To contextualize these human experiences in data, research and analytics, experts at GS&P calculated the estimated number of meals each participant had left with their loved ones – confronting them with the hard truth that our time together is finite. The realization reinforces a poignant reality: the most limited time we have is the time we have together.

The initial shock, as captured in the film, gives way to joy as Rao's surprises participants with an intimate dinner with those they wish they spent more time with, centered around an authentic Rao's Homemade meal. It's a reminder that Rao's products exist to help us slow down, savor the moment, and linger around the table together.

"Rao's has always stood for something bigger than great food. It's about slowing down, gathering around the table, and truly being present with the people we love," said Vikram Singh, SVP, Italian & Frozen Category Leader at The Campbell's Company. "This film is an incredibly powerful reminder that those moments are more limited than we think. My hope is that it inspires all of us to make more time for the people who matter most, and to truly savor those moments when we have them. Because ultimately, the most limited time we have is the time we have together."

The "Limited-Time Only" film anchors a broader body of work created by Goodby Silverstein & Partners, which encompasses four commercial spots and social and influencer content. In a departure from the Italian pastiche common in the category, each commercial has a musical soundtrack that is scored by a live orchestra and elegantly captures the beauty of what happens when we gather around the table, with messaging that inspires viewers to linger a little longer. Each spot ends with a scarpetta, the beloved Italian ritual of sweeping bread through the last of the sauce, a simple gesture that captures what Rao's is all about: taking the time to savor every last bite.

To watch the newly released film, visit Raos.com/LimitedTimeOnly and follow @raoshomemade on Instagram and TikTok.

About The Campbell's Company

For more than 155 years, The Campbell's Company (NASDAQ:CPB) (Campbell's) has been connecting people through food they love. Headquartered in Camden, N.J. since 1869, generations of consumers have trusted us to provide delicious and affordable food and beverages. Today, the company is a North American focused brand powerhouse, generating fiscal 2026 net sales of $9.7 billion across two divisions: Meals & Beverages and Snacks. Our portfolio of 16 leadership brands includes Campbell's, Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pace, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Rao's, Snack Factory, Snyder's of Hanover, Swanson and V8. For more information, visit thecampbellscompany.com.

releases.title: Vancouver, Washington Welcomes Its First Major Cinematic Event at Regal City Center
releases.body:
Vancouver Movie Fête brings three days of movies, diverse programming, and emerging creative talent to downtown Vancouver, September 17–19, 2027.

VANCOUVER, Wash., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vancouver, Washington is preparing to welcome its first major cinematic event at Regal City Center in downtown Vancouver. Vancouver Movie Fête (VMF), a new three-day cinematic event, will take place September 17–19, 2027, bringing an expansive selection of movies, emerging creative talent, and audiences together at one of the city's most recognized entertainment destinations.

The event has secured official sponsorship from Hotel Indigo Vancouver Waterfront and El Gaucho, two prominent names on Vancouver's waterfront. Further strengthening its community foundation, Vancouver Movie Fête has received a $6,000 Inspire Grant from the City of Vancouver, demonstrating the city's support for this new addition to its cultural and entertainment landscape.

A Cinematic Experience for Audiences and Industry Professionals

Vancouver Movie Fête is designed to appeal to a broad audience, from everyday moviegoers to cinephiles, independent creators, and established entertainment industry professionals. While celebrating the artistry and craft of cinematic production, VMF is equally focused on the excitement of the big-screen experience and the audiences who make it possible.

Its programming offers a distinctive mix of genres, including thrillers, horror, dark documentaries, animation, and movies for children. The result is an event that brings together diverse creative perspectives, industry talent, and movie enthusiasts, with something to engage a wide range of audiences.

Investing in the Next Generation of Creators

One of the event's distinguishing features is its Next Gen Filmmaker category, open to young creatives between the ages of 14 and 17.

Selected teenage creators will have their movies screened at Regal City Center as part of the event's official selection. The category provides young storytellers with an opportunity to bring their creative work to a major theater screen and participate in a professionally presented cinematic event alongside other selected productions.

Built From the Ground Up

Founded by Tricia H., Founder and CEO, Vancouver Movie Fête has been developed from the ground up since April 2026.

With a longstanding network of relationships with entertainment industry professionals whose experience includes major studio productions, Tricia has brought together the partnerships, programming, and organizational foundation to establish VMF as a new cinematic destination in Southwest Washington.

The combination of major theater access, waterfront hospitality partnerships, municipal grant support, and programming that reaches beyond traditional industry audiences gives Vancouver Movie Fête a distinctive position in the region's entertainment landscape.

Submissions Now Open

Submissions are currently being accepted through FilmFreeway and Hiike Independent. Creators are invited to submit productions across the event's programming categories for consideration.

The submission deadline is May 31, 2027. Submission does not guarantee official selection.

releases.title: Peak Nano Expands U.S. Capacitor Film Production 20-Fold in Ohio, and Opens Hiring Across Three Shifts
releases.body:
Ohio-invented nanolayer film moves to full-scale production on a new Davis-Standard line; job fair set for Nov. 21

MACEDONIA, Ohio, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Nano today announced a 20-fold expansion of NanoPlex™ HDC capacitor film production at its Macedonia, Ohio, facility, moving its advanced nanolayer dielectric film from early production to full commercial scale. A new Davis-Standard cast film line will add up to three million pounds of annual capacity, serving sectors including the power grid, AI data centers, fusion energy, industrial power, and defense when it reaches full production in the first quarter of 2028. Peak Nano will host a job fair on Saturday, Nov. 21, to fill more than 15 immediate openings for extrusion and inspection technicians across all three shifts, including weekday and weekend hours, with further expansion planned in 2027.

Peak Nano makes the thin plastic film inside capacitors, the parts that store and release an electric field in the power grid, data centers, and defense systems. Where conventional single-polymer films hit their limits on heat, voltage, and lifespan, NanoPlex is engineered with multiple polymers at the nanoscale that work together to store more energy, run cooler, and last longer. It's a drop-in film already in production, helping critical industries power past performance and supply bottlenecks. The new line is the next phase of the company's build-out of U.S. dielectric film production, and the first film extrusion line sited at Roll & Hold, Peak Nano's Macedonia facility.

"We have breakthrough technology. Now we're building the capacity to let the world see it," said Jim Welsh, CEO of Peak Nano. "Northeast Ohio has been building America's polymer industry for more than a century. Expanding NanoPlex production 20-fold in Macedonia is new growth for Ohio, and it puts American-invented, American-made film at the center of a global market that grids, data centers, and defense systems depend on."

Scaling a proven partnership

The new Davis-Standard line will produce mono-, multi-, and nanolayered films, scaling up from the Davis-Standard cast nanolayer line Peak Nano commissioned in 2022. The new film line is expected to be in full production in Q1 2028, and Peak is hiring now to begin training and expand our production team. At full production, this line will produce up to three million pounds of film a year, with a total investment of $20M in equipment, facilities, and staffing.

"This line is a first-of-a-kind for Davis-Standard, as we partner with Peak Nano to deliver our first full-scale production line built for nanolayered films for dielectrics, medical, and food applications. Our teams have worked side by side with Peak Nano since they commissioned the first Davis-Standard line in 2022, and this system takes that work to production scale. We are proud to build it for an American manufacturer supplying the films behind the grid, data centers, and national defense," said Christian Renners, Davis-Standard Business Unit President.

Why now

Demand for capacitor film is climbing as the grid and data center build-out expands. U.S. electricity use is on track for a record 4,288 billion kilowatt-hours in 2026, driven largely by data centers, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The Electric Power Research Institute projects data centers could use 9% to 17% of U.S. electricity by 2030, roughly double today's share. Average capacitor lead times reached 19 weeks in October 2025, 46% above pre-pandemic levels, with film capacitors among the most active categories. Fusion is opening a new market as well: a single pulsed-power fusion facility can require tens of thousands of capacitors, according to TTI MarketEYE.

Ohio-born technology with Federal support

NanoPlex grew out of nanolayer polymer research at Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland, developed with Case Western Reserve, DARPA, and the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory. Peak Nano's science leadership includes Chief Science Officer Dr. Michael Ponting, a Case Western Reserve PhD. Today, NanoPlex HDC is 100% U.S.-engineered and manufactured.

Peak Nano continues to build on Ohio's polymer expertise through the Polymer Industry Cluster, an industry-driven consortium powered by the Greater Akron Chamber. Its Greater Akron Polymer Innovation Hub supports Peak Nano's R&D work on biodegradable nanolayered packaging films.

Peak Nano is also an industry partner in NEO-SMART, the Case Western Reserve-led coalition of more than 70 regional manufacturers and institutions and an NSF Regional Innovation Engine to advance materials and manufacturing innovation. Together, these connections help turn Ohio's research strengths into new technologies, manufacturing capabilities, and jobs.

"Northeast Ohio has been turning polymers into products for more than a century," said Nick Barendt, CEO of NEO-SMART. "Peak Nano shows what that legacy still makes possible: a discovery from a Case Western Reserve lab, scaled into a new production line in Macedonia. NEO-SMART exists to help more companies like Peak Nano take discoveries from the lab to the market, and build them here." 

"Peak Nano is a leader in advanced polymers, and this expansion shows what Ohio's workforce can build," said Congressman Dave Joyce. "As a member of the Defense Appropriations Subcommittee, I have been proud to fight for the federal investments in critical materials technology that make projects like this possible. This new production line will strengthen our domestic supply chain for the materials that underpin our electric grid and key national security capabilities."

Hiring now

Peak Nano will host a job fair on Saturday, Nov. 21, from 9 a.m. to noon at its Valley View facility, 7700 Hub Parkway, Suite 8, Valley View, OH 44125. The event will offer on-site interviews and short guided plant tours. Training is provided for new hires, and veterans are encouraged to apply. Candidates should bring a resume and can learn more and pre-register at https://www.peaknano.com/events/job-fair.

FAQs

Who manufactures advanced capacitor film in the United States?

Peak Nano manufactures NanoPlex™ HDC capacitor film in Northeast Ohio and is the only U.S. manufacturer of nanolayer dielectric film. U.S. production of polypropylene capacitor film ended in 2013, which left capacitor makers relying on suppliers overseas. NanoPlex HDC is 100% U.S.-engineered and manufactured, with a supply chain sourced from allied nations.

Is NanoPlex HDC in commercial production?

Yes. Peak Nano has produced NanoPlex HDC on a Davis-Standard cast nanolayer line since 2022, after more than a decade of development with Case Western Reserve University, DARPA, and the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory. The technology is protected by more than 20 global patents, and every roll is made under ISO 9001 certification, in-line inspection, and lot traceability.

How much capacitor film can Peak Nano supply?

Peak Nano's new Macedonia, Ohio, line will add up to three million pounds of annual capacity at full production in the first quarter of 2028, a 20-fold increase. The company is investing $20 million in equipment, facilities, and staffing. It is hiring and training technicians across three shifts now and plans further expansion in 2027.

Can capacitor manufacturers use NanoPlex HDC in existing designs?

Yes. NanoPlex HDC is a drop-in replacement for conventional capacitor films, so manufacturers can qualify it on existing metallizing and winding equipment without redesigning their capacitors. Peak Nano's applications engineering team supports customers through qualification. Learn more at peaknano.com/nanoplex/hdc.

About Peak Nano

Founded in 2016, Peak Nano engineers and manufactures nanolayer polymer films in Northeast Ohio. Its NanoPlex™ HDC and LDF dielectric films, developed from over a decade of research with Case Western Reserve University, DARPA, and the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory, store and deliver energy in capacitors for the power grid, AI data centers, fusion energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, industrial power, and defense systems. NanoPlex™ technology is protected by more than 20 global patents, designed and engineered in the U.S., with a supply chain sourced from allied nations. Peak Nano's films are drop-in replacements that measurably improve system performance, reduce dependence on foreign suppliers, and strengthen American energy independence, leadership, and national security. Learn more at peaknano.com.

releases.title: The Louisiana First Horizon Foundation Announces Investment in Louisiana Music Museum
releases.body:
LAFAYETTE, La., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Louisiana First Horizon Foundation today announced a significant investment in the Louisiana Music Museum, a program of the Acadiana Center for the Arts. The Foundation's support will help preserve Louisiana's rich musical heritage while advancing the development of a new cultural and educational destination in Downtown Lafayette.

The Foundation's commitment supports the museum's ongoing capital campaign and includes naming recognition for the Walk of Legends Plaza, an outdoor entrance space along South Buchanan Street designed to celebrate Louisiana's musical legends and their contributions to the state's cultural heritage.

"Louisiana's music is an important part of our culture and identity, and the Foundation is proud to support a project that will preserve that legacy for future generations," said Jerry Prejean, Acadiana Market President for First Horizon. "This museum will not only celebrate the artists and traditions that make our state unique, but also create new opportunities for education, tourism and economic growth in the communities we call home."

Located in the historic 1890 Lafayette Hardware Store in Downtown Lafayette, the museum will bring Louisiana's musical history to life through immersive exhibits, storytelling and educational experiences. From Cajun and Creole traditions to jazz, blues, zydeco, gospel, funk and more, the museum will highlight the diverse sounds and artists that have shaped the state's musical identity.

"The Louisiana Music Museum is about more than preserving our musical heritage. It's about bringing to life the stories, traditions and creativity that have shaped Louisiana's rich cultural identity," said Samuel Oliver, Executive Director of Acadiana Center for the Arts. "We hope to create a space that celebrates Louisiana's remarkable contributions to music while inspiring future generations. We're grateful to First Horizon for believing in this vision and helping us bring it to life."

Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with the museum slated to open in 2028.

About the Louisiana First Horizon Foundation

The Louisiana First Horizon Foundation is a private charitable foundation of First Horizon National Corporation. Founded in 2020, the Foundation has donated more than $15 million to meet community needs. Grants from the Foundation support the following impact areas: Arts & Culture, Education & Leadership, Environment, Financial Literacy and Health & Human Services. More information is available at www.firsthorizonfoundation.com

About AcA

As the community leader in arts and culture, the Acadiana Center for the Arts (AcA) serves to bring elevating arts experiences to the people of Acadiana through many approaches including holding public concerts, presenting art exhibitions, providing grants to artists and cultural organizations, and bringing artists into schools across the region. AcA brings equitable access to the arts through year-round education and outreach activities and aims to build a more sustainable cultural ecosystem for future generations in Acadiana. www.acadianacenterforthearts.org.

releases.title: B2K RETURNS WITH ECLIPSE, THE PLATINUM-SELLING R&B GROUP'S FIRST STUDIO ALBUM IN NEARLY 24 YEARS, OUT NOW
releases.body:
Original Members Omarion, J-Boog, Lil' Fizz and Raz-B Reunite on BPC Music Group's Inaugural Album Release

Lead Single "Mileage" Reaches the Top 15 at R&B/Hip-Hop Radio and No. 1 on Apple Music's R&B Songs and R&B Videos Charts. New Single "Co-Sign" Arrives Today

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Platinum-selling R&B group B2K returns today with ECLIPSE, its first studio album in nearly 24 years, via BPC Music Group. Original members Omarion, J-Boog, Lil' Fizz and Raz-B reunite on the thirteen-track project, which arrives alongside the new single "Co-Sign," produced and written by The Underdogs. ECLIPSE is available now on all major streaming platforms. STREAM/PURCHASE LINK

Watch the lyric video for "Co-Sign" here.

The hits. The harmonies. The moves. The brotherhood. B2K helped define a generation of R&B, and ECLIPSE brings four distinct journeys back into one unmistakable sound. The album features production from Sean Garrett, The Underdogs, Troy Taylor, Hitmaka, Blaq Tuxedo, Lil Ronnie, Kenneth "KP" Paige and Ethos, with songwriting contributions from B2K, The Underdogs, Eric Bellinger, Ant Clemons and Tyree Hawkins, among others.

The rollout began in July with "Mileage," which debuted at No. 38 on Billboard's Mainstream R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay chart, marking B2K's first entry on the chart in more than two decades and its seventh career entry. The single climbed to No. 23 on the Billboard tally, reached the Top 15 at R&B/Hip-Hop radio, and hit No. 1 on both Apple Music's R&B Songs and R&B Videos charts.

B2K followed in October with "Lil Freak," an Atlanta bass-inspired track produced by Lil Ronnie, Slikk Muzik and Kelby on the Track. Released with an official visualizer, the track pairs the group's signature vocal chemistry with a bass-heavy groove built for the dance floor.

Ahead of the album's release, B2K celebrated its return with an exclusive performance on NBC's TODAY on November 4, delivering a medley that paired new music from ECLIPSE with the group's signature hits. Find clip here.

"ECLIPSE is a celebration of our brotherhood, growth, and legacy. 25 years later, we're still making history," states Raz B of B2K.

"20+ years later, the stars have aligned. It's been so much fun bringing this project to life, and that energy speaks for itself in every track. Enjoy the music. Get ready for the ECLIPSE. B2K 2026. No, we don't miss," said Omarion of B2K.

"We're proud to share this next chapter with our fans. ECLIPSE is a moment we've all been waiting for!" exclaims Fizz of B2K.

"Being able to reunite with my brothers and give our fans new music after 24 years is something I'm truly proud of," says J Boog of B2K.

ECLIPSE is the inaugural album release from BPC Music Group, the label founded by Black Promoters Collective partners Gary Guidry and Troy Brown. Black Promoters Collective also presented the Boys 4 Life Tour, the nationwide arena run that brought B2K and Bow Wow back together onstage.

"We've worked with B2K on stage for years, and ECLIPSE is the natural next step: new music from four artists who still have plenty to say," said Gary Guidry, CEO of BPC Music Group.

B2K has earned seven Billboard Hot 100 entries, including the No. 1 smash "Bump, Bump, Bump," and two RIAA-certified platinum albums, B2K and Pandemonium! The group's self-titled debut reached No. 1 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart and No. 2 on the Billboard 200.

The group's three BET Awards include the 2002 Viewer's Choice Award for "Uh Huh," followed by Best Group and the Viewer's Choice Award for "Bump, Bump, Bump" in 2003. B2K also earned a Billboard Music Award for R&B/Hip-Hop Single Sales Track of the Year for "Uh Huh," three Soul Train Music Awards for B2K, Pandemonium! and "Bump, Bump, Bump," and a 2003 Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Award for Favorite Music Group.

From "Uh Huh," "Gots Ta Be" and "Why I Love You" to "Girlfriend" and "Bump, Bump, Bump," B2K soundtracked a generation's coming-of-age years. The group's signature choreography and the members' roles in the 2004 dance film You Got Served made them a fixture on screen as well as on the charts. With ECLIPSE, all four members give fans a new reason to turn the volume up.

ABOUT B2K

B2K is an American R&B boy band that rose to prominence in the early 2000s with their smooth vocals, infectious dance routines, and charismatic appeal. Comprised of Omarion, Lil' Fizz, J-Boog, and Raz-B, the group became one of the defining acts of their era with chart-topping hits including "Bump, Bump, Bump," "Uh Huh," "Why I Love You," and "Girlfriend." Their platinum-selling albums B2K and Pandemonium! earned widespread acclaim, including a BET Award for Best Group, Billboard Music Award for R&B/Hip-Hop Single Sales Track of the Year, Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Award for Favorite Music Group and multiple Soul Train Music Awards, while their starring role in the iconic 2004 dance film You Got Served further cemented their place in pop culture. More than two decades after their debut, B2K continues to resonate with audiences across generations, with their successful reunion and sold-out Boys 4 Life Tour reaffirming the group's lasting impact on R&B and their status as one of the most influential boy bands of the early 2000s. The group is currently preparing to release a new album this fall, led by the upcoming single "Mileage," produced by Ethos.

ABOUT BPC MUSIC GROUP

BPC Music Group, established in 2025 by Gary Guidry and Troy Brown, partners in the Black Promoters Collective, was founded on a commitment to artist development, creative freedom, and Black ownership. Dedicated to releasing music that moves culture forward, the label's growing roster includes Bow Wow, whose 2025 single "Use Me," featuring Chris Brown, debuted at No. 1 on the R&B radio chart. BPC Music Group is set to release B2K's highly anticipated first album in over two decades later this year, ushering in the next chapter of one of R&B's most beloved groups.

releases.body:
SOCAN Foundation awards Music Creator Day grants totalling $40,000

Canadians encouraged to celebrate and support the artists, songwriters, and composers behind the music they love

TORONTO, Nov. 6, 2026 /CNW/ -- On the eve of Canada's second annual Music Creator Day, SOCAN is proud to announce the recipients of its inaugural Music Creator Day grants. Through the SOCAN Foundation, a total of $40,000 in grant funding was awarded to four Canadian organizations whose projects showcase or invest in the work of music creators. 

Established alongside Music Creator Day in 2025 and celebrated each year on November 7 in honour of legendary Canadian songwriter Joni Mitchell's birthday, these grants support organizations that help songwriters and composers develop their craft and connect with audiences.

Together, the grant recipients represent a diverse range of projects that reflect the spirit of Music Creator Day through performances, educational programming, mentorship opportunities, and community-focused initiatives.

"Music Creator Day was established to recognize the cultural contributions of songwriters and composers at home and abroad," said Charlie Wall-Andrews, Executive Director, SOCAN Foundation. "These grants bring that vision to life by supporting organizations that create opportunities for music creators to learn and grow. We're proud to celebrate organizations investing in the careers of Canadian music creators."

"The goal of Music Creator Day is simple: to celebrate the songwriters and composers whose work makes our lives better. By shining a spotlight on music creators, we're building greater appreciation for the talent and creativity at the very heart of Canadian music," said Jennifer Brown, SOCAN CEO.

OPELIKA, Ala., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bass Pro Shops Bulls, Bands, & Barrels announced its 19-stop national tour for 2027, featuring its first stadium event March 5 and 6 at Lourdes Stadium in Lafayette, Louisiana. Jason Aldean and Treaty Oak Revival will headline the two-day event.

Aldean will headline Friday, March 5, followed by Treaty Oak Revival on Saturday, March 6. The two-day event, billed as Battle in the Boot, brings bull riding, barrel racing and freestyle bullfighting together with live country music. Additional performers include Lauren Alaina and Fox N' Vead. Hotel packages, RV parking, tailgating and more will give fans new ways to make BBB's stadium debut a country music and western sports getaway.

BBB's signature arena show packs bull riding, barrel racing, freestyle bullfighting and live country music into a three-hour spectacle built for longtime fans and first-timers alike. The competition and concert share the spotlight, bringing four distinct attractions together for one unforgettable night out.

Fans can take their BBB experience beyond the grandstands with Pit Passes and Behind the Chutes Tours, available as add-ons in every market. Pit Passes offer front-of-stage access for the concert, while Behind the Chutes Tours take fans to the bucking chutes for an inside look at the sport and opportunities to meet the athletes, cast and crew who bring BBB to life.

Fans can register for presale access at BullsBandsAndBarrels.com. Presale for select tour dates begins Thursday, Nov. 12, with public ticket sales beginning Friday, Nov. 13. Ticketing details for the BBB Finals and the stops on May 1 and May 15 will be announced separately.

"The music matters as much as what happens in the dirt," said Hunter Price, founder and CEO of Bulls, Bands, & Barrels. "Lafayette takes that whole experience into a stadium for two days, with Jason Aldean and Treaty Oak Revival leading the lineup. We're giving fans a reason to make a weekend of it. This ain't your grandpappy's rodeo."

The tour opens Jan. 9 at Ford Center in Evansville, Indiana, and runs through June. Artists appearing on selected dates include Jon Pardi, Parker McCollum, Tucker Wetmore, Sam Barber, Kameron Marlowe, Ole 60, Vincent Mason, Dexter and The Moonrocks, and more. Lineups vary by market.

The season culminates June 4 and 5 with the two-night BBB Finals, where athletes from across the tour will compete for championship titles.

The 2027 season marks a new partnership with Doussan Music Group, an independent concert promotion and live entertainment company, to support the continued growth of BBB.

"BBB has built a strong identity by giving the competition and the concert equal billing," said Russell Doussan, founder and CEO of Doussan Music Group. releases.title: COUNTRY MUSIC STAR WYNONNA JUDD TO BE HONORED WITH PRESTIGIOUS ASCAP GOLDEN NOTE AWARD
releases.body:
The five-time Grammy-winning Country Music Hall of Fame member has earned 19 #1 singles as a solo artist and with The Judds

NEW YORK, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ASCAP, the American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers, will honor country music star Wynonna Judd with the ASCAP Golden Note Award.

Past ASCAP Golden Note honorees include Garth Brooks, Tom Petty, LeAnn Rimes, Lee Ann Womack, Reba and Alan Jackson.

The ASCAP Golden Note Award celebrates extraordinary career milestones achieved by songwriters, composers and artists. Past honorees include Garth Brooks, Tom Petty, LeAnn Rimes, Lee Ann Womack, Reba, Alan Jackson and Don Williams, among others.

"Wynonna's legendary career is defined by a singular, powerhouse voice and a rich body of work that has permanently shaped the landscape of American music," said ASCAP Chairman of the Board and President Paul Williams. "As we honor her with the ASCAP Golden Note Award, we celebrate a true trailblazer whose soulful, unmistakable sound continues to inspire generations of music creators."

With the release of her 1992 self-titled solo debut, Wynonna emerged as an exceptional force in American music. Beyond five Grammy Awards, multi-platinum albums and sold-out tours, the country/soul vocalist built on the Appalachian traditionalism that defined The Judds to create a world where a top 5 dance/club hit was as possible as being inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Having practically grown up as America's favorite musical daughter, Wynonna matured into a woman who embraced how life is filled with peaks and valleys, great thrills and heavy disappointment. Those realities informed her five-times platinum Wynonna and platinum-selling Tell Me Why, albums that gave voice to every human being emerging into adulthood with joy in their heart. Beyond the groundbreaking music she and her mother created as The Judds, Wynonna has grown into her once-in-a-generation vocal prowess with an ease that made people flock to her. "No One Else on Earth," "Tell Me Why," "She Is His Only Need," "Girls with Guitars" and "I Saw the Light" set the next chapter in motion for the girl from Ashland, Kentucky who became a global superstar.

Most recently, Wynonna released The Hard Truth (via ANTI-Records). The 10-track project was her first time co-writing an album – one that masterfully weaves her own painful trials with resounding joy and triumph. In its first week, the album garnered over 1.3 million streams and debuted in the top 10 on Billboard's Top Album Sales chart. Wynonna is currently on the road on The Hard Truth Tour, a 33-date tour that brings her unmistakable voice, powerhouse performances and deeply personal new music to audiences across North America.

The award will be presented at the ASCAP Nashville Songwriters Celebration on Monday, November 16 in Nashville. The invitation-only celebration recognizes the songwriters and publishers of the past year's most-performed ASCAP country and Christian songs.

About ASCAP

The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a membership association of more than 1.1 million songwriters, composers and music publishers, and represents some of the world's most talented music creators. Founded and governed by songwriters, composers and publishers, it returns nearly 90 cents of every dollar collected to its members as royalties and has the lowest overhead of any U.S. PRO. ASCAP licenses a repertory of over 20 million musical works to hundreds of thousands of businesses that use music, including streaming services, cable television, radio and satellite radio and brick and mortar businesses such as retail stores, hotels, clubs, restaurants and bars. ASCAP collects the licensing fees, and identifies, matches, processes and pays royalties to its members for trillions of performances every year. The ASCAP blanket license offers an efficient solution for businesses to legally perform ASCAP music while respecting the right of songwriters and composers to be paid fairly. ASCAP puts music creators first, advocating for their rights and the value of music on Capitol Hill, driving innovation that moves the industry forward, building community and providing the resources and support that creators need to succeed in their careers. Learn more and stay in touch at www.ascap.com, on X and Instagram @ASCAP and on Facebook.

releases.title: iQIYI Revives 90-Year-Old Lost Film with NadouPro, Shortlisted for the AI Unit at the Golden Rooster Awards
releases.body:
BEIJING, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- iQIYI, China's leading online entertainment platform, is pioneering a new path in AI-powered film restoration through NadouPro, the company's AI platform built for professional film and television production. NadouPro has enabled the creative restoration of "Visiting Shanghai after Sixty Years", a short film lost for nearly 90 years. This shows how AI can restore films with almost no surviving original footage, bringing them back to life.

Completed by an eight-person team at the iQIYI-XMU Joint Laboratory of Film Restoration in just two months, the project has recently been shortlisted for the "2026 Future Images AI Unit" at the 39th Golden Rooster Awards. The Golden Rooster Awards are among China's most prestigious film honors, underscoring the project's industry recognition.

The Challenge: Building a Movie Without Footage

Traditional film restoration typically relies on surviving film materials, using digital technologies to repair damage and enhance image quality. However, with the original 1938 release of "Visiting Shanghai after Sixty Years" – one of China's earliest science-fiction works, which used comedy to imagine life sixty years into the future – there was almost nothing left to repair. All physical prints, reels, and scripts had been lost over the decades. Instead, the team had to generate the film from scratch using only production still-photos, posters, and newspaper clippings as conceptual guides.

"NadouPro allowed us to step outside the conventional restoration mindset," said Zidong JIANG, Member of iQIYI-XMU Joint Laboratory and iQIYI's Director of AI Restoration Technology. "With no surviving film prints to restore, we used AI to undertake a creative reconstruction of the film based on available historical materials."

Building a film from the ground up highlighted two major complexities in generative video: maintaining character consistency across scenes and achieving precise camera control. The team utilized NadouPro to address both.

Maintaining Continuity Through Digital Assets

The film spans two distinct historical eras – 1938 and 1998 – and features multiple characters. In generative video, ensuring characters retain the same appearance across different shots is historically difficult.

NadouPro solved this by acting as a centralized production hub. Rather than generating characters anew for every scene, the team used the platform to lock in permanent digital assets for each character's facial features, proportions, and costumes upfront. Subsequent shots drew from these foundational files, keeping character appearances perfectly consistent throughout the film.

Enabling Directorial Control with 3D Director Studio

Recreating acting performances from still photos required high precision. Rather than relying on trial-and-error AI generation, the team used NadouPro's 3D Director Studio to precisely control character positioning, composition, and movement, supported by tools for exploring different scenes, visual styles, and camera angles.

This control ensured filmmakers led the creative direction. The 1938 sequences drew inspiration from early black-and-white cinema with stable cameras and vintage lighting, while the 1998 scenes adopted a documentary style with natural light and handheld camera movement.

"NadouPro helped us move from relatively random image generation toward shots with clear directorial intent," said Enji YANG, the Director of the new film. "In the early stage, we still followed traditional methods: script analysis, character design, scene design, and storyboard planning. We always believe the audiovisual design of a film must come first, before considering how AI can realize it."

Aigong ZHANG, Chief Planner of the new film and Director of the iQIYI-XMU Joint Laboratory, noted that the project demonstrates how AI can integrate into a professional workflow. "NadouPro shares something in common with the production of this short film: the organic integration of traditional filmmaking craftsmanship with AI."

Building on Years of AI Restoration Work

As one of the earliest long-form video platforms to invest in AI film restoration, iQIYI has been exploring the related technology since 2017. Its proprietary ZoomAI uses algorithms for scratch repair, super-resolution, noise reduction, and intelligent frame interpolation, helping shift restoration from manual frame-by-frame work toward automated processes.

Through its joint laboratory with Xiamen University, iQIYI has already brought a number of 4K classics back to screens. Building on this experience, iQIYI is now exploring new possibilities beyond traditional film restoration, using AI to creatively reconstruct and reimagine lost films based on surviving historical materials, bringing classic works back to audiences in new forms.
